The department email list was never designed for operational intelligence.

Writing up a brief takes thirty minutes. Routing it to the right people takes guesswork. Officers miss updates buried in an inbox with no read receipts and no accountability. Supervisors have no visibility into what was read, by whom, and when. Every agency knows the problem. Nobody has built a system designed to fix it, until now.

How it works

An intelligence workflow, not just a distribution tool.

AI Brief Drafting
Drop in a report narrative, CAD notes, a PDF, or a photo of a handwritten note. The AI reads it and produces a structured draft tailored to the content type. The supervisor reviews, edits if needed, and publishes. Nothing goes live without human approval.
Intelligent Routing
After a brief is drafted, the AI recommends who should receive it based on district references, content type, current shift data, and recent call history. The supervisor approves or adjusts before publishing. The right brief reaches the right officers, not everyone.
Structured Feed with Change Summaries
ATIs, ATLs, RFIs, CIAC bulletins, stolen vehicles, directed patrol — each content type in its own lane. When a brief is updated, the AI generates a "what changed" summary for every officer who already read the prior version. No rereading from the top to find out what is new.
Natural-Language Search and Feed Quality
Search the archive in plain language. Every result links back to a source brief with author, timestamp, and version. In the background, AI monitors the feed for duplicates, stale briefs, and related series — surfacing findings to supervisors so the feed stays current, uncluttered, and trusted.
